outputs.L2: We establish a criterion that is both necessary and sufficient for the existence of a \(\tilde G_2\)-structure on a compact \(7\)-manifold. This result also yields a sufficient criterion ensuring that an open \(7\)-manifold carries a closed \(3\)-form of \(\tilde G_2\)-type.
outputs.L3: The work establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for a compact seven-dimensional manifold to admit a \(\tilde G_2\)-structure, providing a complete characterization in the compact case. As a consequence, it also gives a sufficient condition for an open seven-manifold to carry a closed differential 3-form of \(\tilde G_2\)-type. Thus, the results address both the existence of \(\tilde G_2\)-structures on compact 7-manifolds and the construction of closed \(\tilde G_2\)-type 3-forms in the open setting.
outputs.L4:
This work studies the existence of \(\tilde G_2\)-structures on smooth 7-manifolds, where \(\tilde G_2\) denotes the split real form of the exceptional Lie group \(G_2\). Such a structure may be described by a differential 3-form lying pointwise in the open \(GL(7,\mathbb R)\)-orbit whose stabilizer is \(\tilde G_2\). By translating this reduction of the frame bundle into topological data associated with the tangent bundle, the work derives a necessary and sufficient condition for a compact 7-manifold to admit a \(\tilde G_2\)-structure. This yields a complete existence criterion in the closed case and clarifies the relationship between split \(G_2\)-geometry and the topology of the underlying manifold.

The noncompact case is treated from the stronger perspective of closed defining forms. For open 7-manifolds, the work establishes a sufficient topological condition ensuring the existence of a closed 3-form of \(\tilde G_2\)-type. The argument uses the flexibility available on open manifolds, allowing an appropriate nondegenerate 3-form to be deformed into one satisfying the closedness equation while preserving its pointwise algebraic type. Consequently, the results extend the existence theory beyond compact manifolds and provide a broad class of noncompact 7-manifolds carrying closed split-\(G_2\) structures.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise abstract stating the existence criterion for $\tilde G_2$-structures on compact 7-manifolds and the consequence for open 7-manifolds.
counterfactuals.output: A compact smooth \(7\)-manifold admits a \(\tilde G_{2}\)-structure precisely when it is orientable and spin, equivalently when \(w_{1}(M)=w_{2}(M)=0\). Consequently, every open orientable spin \(7\)-manifold admits such a structure; by the \(h\)-principle, it may moreover be represented by a closed stable \(3\)-form of split \(G_{2}\)-type.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Provide a brief research summary mentioning both the necessary-and-sufficient condition for compact manifolds and the sufficient condition for closed 3-forms on open manifolds.
counterfactuals.output:
For a smooth compact \(7\)-manifold, the existence of a \(G_2\)-structure—equivalently, a positive stable \(3\)-form—is characterized exactly by
\[
w_1(M)=w_2(M)=0,
\]
i.e. \(M\) is orientable and spin. On an open \(7\)-manifold, an \(h\)-principle strengthens this: the same topological condition is sufficient to obtain a **closed** positive \(3\)-form, hence a closed \(G_2\)-structure. This does not imply a comparable criterion for closed or torsion-free \(G_2\)-structures on compact manifolds.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
